chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, and Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, who said:

I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) oiling with gillyflower oil, so he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Oil (yourself).' So I said to him (peace be upon him): 'What is your stance regarding the violet (oil), and what has been reported with regards to it from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I dislike its smell.' I said to him (peace be upon him): 'So I also disliked its smell, and I disliked saying that to you due to what reached me regarding it from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using violet oil according to Imam al-Askari?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the distinction between *karahah* (dislike/preference) and *haram* (prohibition) in Shia jurisprudence, showing how the Imam’s personal aversion to violet oil did not restrict its permissibility for others. It highlights the scholarly principle that a companion’s hesitation due to reported preferences of the Imam does not equate to a binding legal ruling, emphasizing the importance of distinguishing between personal taste and divine law. The narrative also reflects the practical social dynamics of the time, where companions carefully navigated their actions based on the Imam's known habits.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, and Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jaham who said,

‘I saw Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> oiling with the gillyflower oil, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Oil (yourself)’. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Where do you<sup>asws</sup> stand about the violet (oil) and what has been reported with regards to it, from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> dislike its smell’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So I (also) did not like its smell and I did not like to say that to you<sup>asws</sup> due to what has reached me with regards to it from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father and ibn Faddal from al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm who has said the following: “I once saw abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, apply gillyflower oil and said to me to apply it.’

I then said, ‘Why do you not apply viola oil when there is narration about it from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam :?’ He, abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘I do not like its smell.’ He (the narrator) has said that I said, ‘I also do not like its smell, but I do not like to say it because of the narration from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about it.’ He, abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
